completion of the HR Transformation exercise and the details of its outcome. 
 
SUPPORTING COMMUNITY RADIO MOVEMENT IN INDIA 
8. The Committee note that the Community Radio is an important third -tier 
Radio in Radio Broadcasting, distinct from Public Service Radio broadcasting 
and Commercial Radio. Community Radio Stations (CRSs) are low -power Radio 
Stations, which are meant to be set up and operated by local communities. In 
December 2002, the Government of India approved a policy for the grant of 
license, for setting up of CRS, to well established educational institutions. The CR 
provides a platform for communities to air local voices on issues concerning 
health, nutrition, education, agriculture etc. The Scheme (Supporting Community 
Radio Movement in India) aims to strengthen new and existing CRSs with 
resources, capacity and technology so as to upgrade the standard of the stations 
and increase its reach and visibility to the interior regions of India. The 
Committee are given to understand that the Scheme has been revised ‘wherein it 
is proposed to extend for the period from 2026-27 to 2030 -31 with a total 
proposed allocation of Rs. 50 crore. The thrust areas under the Scheme are (i) to 
increase the number of stations in CR dark areas and (ii) to have at least one 
Community Radio Station in each district of the Country. At present, 560 CRS are 
operational in India (till January, 2026). With respect to budgetary allocations and 
expenditure, the Committee note that Rs. 8.00 crore has been allocated for the FY 
2026-27 (at BE stage). During the FY 2025-26, the BE and RE allocations were Rs. 
17.40 crore and Rs. 8.00 crore , respectively, and the actual expenditure till 8 th 
January, 2026 was Rs. 4.52 crore which is 56.50 % of RE allocations.   
 
          Initiatives taken under the Scheme ‘Supporting Community Radio 
Movement in India’ include organization of National and Regional Sammelans, 
awareness workshops in CR dark areas, etc. However, the Committee find that 
fund utilization has been uneven over the years, and Demand for Grants remains 
limited due to lack of awareness among potential beneficiaries. The Committee , 
therefore, urge the Ministry to streamline grant disbursement, strengthen 
capacity-building programs for CRS staff and provide technical support to 

73 
 
enhance operational efficiency. The Committee, also desire to be apprised of the 
action taken in respect of the following:- (i) Ensure optimum utilistion of allocated 
funds during the FY 2026-27; (ii) Prepare a definite timeline/roadmap and intensify 
efforts for ensuring at least one Community Radio Station in each district, 
particularly CR dark areas,  as per the vision under the Scheme; (iii) Explore the 
feasibility of having one dedicated training cell for CRS personnel in each 
State/Zone to improve technical skills, content creation and community 
engagement; and (iv) Involve local Government, educational institutions, NGOs, 
and community organizations to promote awareness and local participation. 
 
FILM SECTOR  
 
NATIONAL CENTRE OF EXCELLENCE (NCOE) FOR ANIMATION, VISUAL 
EFFECTS (VFX), GAMING, COMICS AND EXTENDED REALITY (AVGC-XR) 
 
9. The Committee note that the AVGC Promotion Task Force was set up by 
the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting in April 2022 after the Union Budget 
announcement and the Task Force submitted its report in December 2022, 
recommending a National AVGC Mission, Centres of Excellence, stronger 
infrastructure and dedicated support for Indian IP and exports.   IICT Mumbai has 
been established and is being developed as a specialised Centre of Excellence to 
strengthen high -end training and research. With a focus on expanding high -
quality production capacity, developing talent and improving access to 
international markets, WAVES  2025 was organised in May, 2025 as a global 
platform for the entire Media & Entertainment sector. Three verticals of WAVES 
platform that are supporting the AVGC sector are (i) WAVES Bazaar - an year -
round, hybrid global marketplace for India’s media and entertainment sector. It 
enables structured B2B meetings, co -production deals and showcasing of Indian 
films, animation, gaming, VFX and XR content to  international buyers; (ii) WAVEX 
- A dedicated startup accelerator and incubator for AVGC-XR and emerging media 
technologies. It provides early -stage studios access to mentorship, advanced 
production and immersive -tech infrastructure, and curated investor linkages to 
help them scale and secure global projects. At WAVES Summit 2025, it facilitated 
pitching for 30 startups to investors while providing exhibition space for over 100 
startups to engage with international studios. Through partnerships with T -Hub 
and IICT, it currently incubates startups, supports Government pilots via 
innovation challenges like Bhashasetu, and provides  global exposure through 
platforms like IFFI, successfully aiding startups in securing foreign investment 

74 
 
and validating Indian IP abroad; (iii) Creatosphere - Annual ‘Create in India 
challenges’ that runs 30 –35 national competitions across animation, gaming, 
webtoons and digital story  telling. It serves as a talent -discovery platform, 
nurturing new creators and connecting them with mentorship, incubation and 
industry opportunities. Year-wise proposed targets for IICT/WAVES, furnished by 
the Ministry, include (a) IICT, Mumbai to be recognized Deemed University under 
‘Distinct Institution’ category focusing on 17 specialized courses across 
Animation, VFX, Gaming, and Comics during the FY 2026 -27; (b) IICT, Mumbai to 
be located in its permanent campus and established as a complete university, 
and WAVES, 2027 during the FY 2027 -28; and  (c) IICT, Mumbai to fully function 
as the hub of AVGC -XR in India, during the FY 2028 -29.  The Ministry conveyed 
that these initiatives collectively support the formulation of a structured policy 
and guideline framework for the AVGC -XR sector. Further, a dedicated mission 
for Media and Entertainment Sector (including AVGC Sector) is also under its 
consideration. 
 
With regard to harnessing benefits of AI in the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting, on content creation, programming and broadcasting, the Ministry 
submitted that under the WAVES Platform, WaveX (A high -intensity accelerator 
connecting Al -focussed M&E startups with global capital) has launched ‘Kalaa 
Setu’ and ‘Bhasha Setu’ to invite AI startups to build a real -time multilingual 
multimedia content generation solution for prompt citizen outreach. Under Kalaa 
Setu and Bhasha Setu, 10 startups have been selected, and their AI -enabled 
services are currently being utilized on a pilot basis by various media units, 
including the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Central Bureau of Communication 
(CBC), Doordarshan (DD), Akashvani, New Media Wing, and Publications 
Division. The services being tested include translation of press releases and 
articles into regional languages, video creation, subtitle generation, voice -overs, 
e-Books, audio books, audio dubbing in regional languages  etc. Based on the 
outcomes of the p ilot, a limited RFP is proposed to be floated shortly for 
empanelling the selected startups to provide AI -based services to these media 
units on a regular basis. Further, positioning WAVES as a platform for 
“entertainment economics and technology”, MoI&B has launched Creatosphere 
(An Al -driven immersion and co -creation zone), which is part of the broader 
ecosystem for tech (including AI) adoption in M&E. Besides, under Doordarshan, 
DD News have constituted a Committee to explore and evaluate various 

75 
 
opportunities for integrating AI technologies into the channel operations. 
Potential applications under consideration include AI anchors, voice -over 
services, and other innovative uses of Artificial Intelligence that could enhance 
content delivery and audience engagement.  
The Committee note that with rapidly evolving technology and increasing 
internet penetration all across the Country, coupled with one of the cheapest data 
rates, the usage of AVGC -XR globally is poised to grow at an exponential pace.  
This creates abundant opportunities, particularly through the National Centre of 
Excellence [(NCoE)/ Indian Institute of Creative Technology (IICT)] which has 
some key objectives like (a) Focus sing of creating Indian IP; (b) Leveraging our 
cultural heritage in new age; (c) Create a multiplier effect in the industry; (d) An 
industry led initiative in partnership with State and academia; (e) Integrated focus 
on education, skilling industry, development, innovation; (f) Hub and spoke 
model of development to be followed; and (g) IIIC as the hub and several cent ers 
as its spokes dedicated innovation and research fund to promote start -up 
ecosystem. The Committee note that this year's Budget announcement under the 
banner of Indian Institute of Creative Technology for 15,000 Content Creation 
Labs, and objectives under NCoE will play a significant role to allow our creators 
to gain access to the latest tools and technologies, generate employment and 
boost ‘Orange Economy’ of the Country.  
Considering that AVGC -XR sector is emerging as a critical pillar of the 
Creative Economy/Orange Economy, the Committee hope that the initiatives 
undertaken by the Ministry under this sector will harness the potential of the 
Indian AVGC-XR industry and urge the Ministry to: - (i) Ensure  that the timeline 
and targets fixed for NCoE/IICT/WAVES are adhered to and the Committee may be 
apprised of the tangible outcome of the initiatives taken under this Sector;  (ii) 
Finalize a National AVGC -XR Mission/Policy at the earliest with clear objectives, 
measurable targets, institutional responsibilities, and funding provisions to 
ensure sustained growth of the AVGC -XR sector; (iii) To complete the proposed 
permanent campus of IICT at Film City, Goregaon, on schedule;  (iv) Link Talent 
Discovery to Commercial Viability under the ‘Talent Development in Animation, 
Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics (AVGC) Sector’ component (under the Central 
Sector Scheme – DCDFC); (v) Promote Indian IP and Original Content in 
animation, gaming, VFX and XR by providing financial incentives, co -production 
frameworks, and export promotion schemes  to reduce dependency on 
outsourced work from global studios;  (vi)  Establish additional regional Centres 

76 
 
of Excellence in collaboration with States, industry and academic institutions to 
create a distributed skill development and research ecosystem to fix year -wise 
and quarter -wise targets for each of the initiatives taken/planned under AVGC 
Sector; (vii) Furnish details with respect to establishment of Animation, Visual 
Effects, Gaming and Comics (AVGC) Content Creator Labs in 15,000 schools and 
500 colleges, as announced in Budget 2026–27 under WAVES/IICT; (viii) Focus on 
developing a comprehensive curriculum and advanced world -class infrastructure 
for filling up the critical skill gaps in the sector;  (ix) Furnish details of the 
States/UTs who participated in WAVES Summit and those selected to b e part of 
the WAVES vision; (x) Make WaveX and WAVES Bazaar initiatives as continuous 
platforms to have support through  out the year for incubation, mentorship, 
funding, and global market access for startups, rather than  limiting them to 
annual events; and (xi) The Committee are of the view that the  Ministry may 
consider formulating clear guidelines to ensure the ethical and responsible use of 
Artificial Intelligence in broadcasting, particularly in the use of AI -based news 
anchors. The Committee urge that  AI should be deployed as a complementary 
tool rather than a replacement for human professionals, ensuring that 
technological adoption does not lead to job displacement of one and giving it to 
some other. The Committee are of the opinion that a dequate policy measures 
may also be devised to protect and promote human creativity, especially in 
journalism, films, music and other creative fields so as to ensure that 
technological advancements do not undermine human talent and artistic 
excellence. 
 
INFORMATION SECTOR  
 
Press Information Bureau (PIB) 
10. The Committee note that the Press Information Bureau (PIB) is the nodal 
agency of the Government of India to disseminate information through print, 
electronic and social media on Government policies  and programmes, initiatives 
and achievements. It functions as an interface between the Government and the 
media and also provides feedback to the Government on people’s reaction as 
reflected in the media. It also advises the Government on communication 
strategies best suited to meet the needs of the media.  Unde r PIB, a Fact Check 
Unit (FCU) was set up in November, 2019, in order to monitor and check the 
circulation and dissemination of factually incorrect/doctored news and 
information over different modes of news media and social media platforms, 

77 
 
which often mislead people on various issues. The mandate of the PIB Fact 
Check Unit is to provide the official/authentic version of any news doing rounds 
on various media platforms by making available the factually correct information 
in the public domain. The PIB -FCU receives communication/messages from the 
public at large through WhatsApp, email, Twitter and PIB’s website. These fact -
checks are available at the website of PIB. The fact -checked content by PIB -FCU 
is taken up with the concerned social media platforms for appropriate action 
under rule 3(1)(b) of the IT Rules, 2021. Briefing about the Fact Check Unit of PIB, 
the Ministry informed that during Operation Sindoor, the Fact Check Unit of PIB 
worked round the clock to curb fake news, quickly detected and issued swift 
rebuttals to edited videos, misinformation, and propaganda and around 1,400 
URLs were blocked. The Committee are informed that the central Fact -Check Unit 
which falls under the guidelines of the Information Technology (IT) Act, is under 
judicial review. However, a Fact Check Unit under the Press Information Bureau 
(PIB) is currently functional.  
While Clarifying about the mandate of MIB, the Ministry submitted that 
under the IT Act and the Intermediary Guidelines they deal with IT content and 
media content connected with news and media outlets and to that extent, they 
make use of the relevant provisions for removing content under certain 
considerations. The Ministry further admitted the existence of regulatory gaps in 
respect of online media and OTT platforms.  On a related issue, the Ministry 
stated that during the last year, on the basis of Section 294  of the ‘Bharatiya 
Nyaya Sanhita’ Act and Section 4 of the ‘Indecent Representation of Women Act’ , 
25 OTT platforms were blocked initially, and subsequently another 18 platforms 
were blocked. At present, blocking orders are continuously being issued against 
OTT apps and content circulating in online media. In the light of the role and 
mandate of PIB-FCU, the Committee are of the view that the increasing spread of 
misinformation and manipulated content across various media platforms 
necessitates strengthenin g of institutional mechanisms for timely verification , 
quick detection and blocking of fake news, harmful content  and dissemination of 
authentic information. Accordingly, the Committee seek that the following areas 
may also be explored and apprise d them of the outcome: - (i) To enhance the 
outreach and accessibility of the Fact Check Unit under the  PIB through wider 
public awareness campaigns and improved coordination with social media 
platforms; (ii) To enhance technological capabilities, including the use of artificial 
intelligence tools for real -time monitoring of misinformation trends, improved 

78 
 
coordination with social media platforms to facilitate faster identification and 
removal of misleading content;   (iii) Expand the Fact Check Unit’s capacity   with 
quantifiable target for the next FY including trained personnel for regional 
languages; (iv) Publish quarterly transparency reports  on misinformation 
identified, corrective action taken, and engagement with media platforms;  (v) 
Formulate a comprehensive regulatory framework to effectively address issues 
relating to misinformation, harmful content and public grievances related to it , 
coordinate with other Ministries and MeitY  to close regulatory gaps;  and (vi) 
Develop a structured grievance redressal mechanism for online and OTT content, 
integrating Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act and existing civil redress provisions. 
 
NORTH EASTERN REGION (NER) 
11. The Committee note that the budgetary allocations for the FY 2026-27, has 
been fixed at Rs. 111.21 crore at BE stage. The budgetary allocations for NER 
during the financial year 2025 -26 at BE and RE stage, were Rs. 111.85 crore and 
Rs. 117.84 crore respectively. Whereas the actual expenditure, till 31 st December, 
2025, was Rs. 30.71 crore which is just about 26.16% of RE allocations. Under the 
Schemes/Projects/Organisations of the Ministry of Information Broadcasting in 
North Eastern Region, a trend of under -utilisation of funds has been observed 
during the financial years 2022 -23, 2024-25 and 2025 -26.  Regarding the reasons 
for low expenditure during the FY 2025 -26, the Ministry ha ve informed that it 
happened due to multiple factors including (a) On 12.09.2025 withdrawal of BE 
allocations for FY 2025 -26 for the components ‘Continuing Projects of three year 
BIND scheme (2017 -20) to be completed’ in Project Mode and it was later 
reinstated on 16.10.2025; (b) under DCFDC, receipt of limited number of 
proposals from the North East Districts. Also, as per the directives, NFDC was to 
limit its investment to 40% of the production cost. Hence, in regions like NER, for 
producers to invest the remaining 60% or more was challenging; (c) Under CRS, 
there was a very low level of awareness about CRS in the region, consequently 
the numbers of operational  community radio  stations in the region were very 
less.   
With respect to initiatives planned for better performance under the 
Schemes/projects being implemented in North -East Region for the FY 2026 -27, 
the Ministry have informed: (a) Under BIND scheme, the frequency of monitoring 
meetings has been increased at all levels, an Apex Committee has been 
constituted to monitor the progress of projects under the Scheme; (b) under 

79 
 
DCDFC scheme, several measures have been taken for promotion and production 
of feature films, documentaries, animation films in various North Eastern 
languages; (c) under CRS, financial assistance are given to Operational 
Community Radio Stations for purchase of equipment to set -up Community 
Radio Stations, Workshops are held since a significant barrier to the expansion of 
Community Radio Stations (CRSs) across India is that eligible organizations don’t 
know about what community radio is or how it works. The purpose of such 
workshops are spreading awareness among  eligible organizations; (d) under 
DCID, Regions/Units-wise Annual and Quarterly targets are set up; etc. 
In the light of above, the Committee are of the view that  under-utilisation 
undermines the very objective of promoting media infrastructure and cultural 
outreach in the North Eastern Region. The Committee , therefore,  urge the 
Ministry to take  positive action with respect to the following and apprise them 
accordingly:- (i) Prepare a time-bound action plan for optimum utilisation of funds 
allocated under all the schemes of the North Eastern Region (NER);  (ii) Prepare a 
road map with timeline for having at least one Community Radio Station (CRS) in 
each district of the North Eastern States as per the vision under supporting 
Community Radio Movement in India and take concrete steps accordingly. Also 
increase awareness among eligible institutions ensuring timely financial 
assistance to establish CRS and to have mechanism for impact assessment;  (iii) 
Upgrade technical infrastructure, including studios, transmitters, and digital 
broadcasting equipment, to improve signal quality and reach in remote and tribal 
areas; and (iv) Intensify outreach efforts, organise more awareness programmes 
and extend necessary facilitation support so that stakeholders/producers from 
the NER are encouraged to actively participate in such initiatives. Also explore 
the possibility of having regional training hubs  in collaboration with IICT and 
other media institutions to strengthen skill development in NER. 
 
LIVE EVENT DEVELOPMENT CELL (LEDC) 
 
12. The Committee do take note  of the initiative of the Ministry of Information 
and Broadcasting to establish the Live Event Development Cell (LEDC), as a joint 
working platform involving various Ministries, State Governments, and industry 
stakeholders to promote the emerging ‘concert economy’ in the Country.  This 
being a nascent industry, growing at a rate of about 20 per cent seems to have 
the potential to generate local employment, boost tourism and contribute to the 
creative economy. The Ministry have informed that they have already held three 

80 
 
meetings of the Joint Working Group, the beta version of the single -window 
portal has been launched and ten event venues related to the live -event concert 
economy are using the portal. The Committee do take cognizance of the 
approach of the Ministry to have (a) a single -window clearance mechanism; (b) 
introducing the concept of pre -approved venues for sports venues, (c) preparing 
an SOP for available venues so that the live event industry can access pre -
approved venues; (d) collaborating with other Ministries for skill development in 
the live events sector; (e) engagement with State Governments to facilitate their 
development of dedicated venues for live events, etc,.  However, in order to 
ensure the objective of positioning India as a global hub for concerts and live 
events is achieved, the Committee urge the Ministry to take action on the 
following and apprise of the progress made in operationalising the Live Event 
Development Cell:-  (i) To take expeditious and timely steps to operationalise the 
single-window clearance portal on a full -scale basis;  (ii) To ensure that all 
relevant Ministries and statutory authorities are integrated with the platform and 
have effective coordination amongst multiple related stakeholders, (iii) To 
prepare the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)  in consultation with the 
States/UTs and concerned agencies; and  (iv) To design specialised training 
programmes for building skilled workforce for the live events industry and 
strengthen collaboration with the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship.
